p: Zulfiqar Khan was born Muhammad Ismail, in 1649 according to the historian Satish Chandra or in 1657 according to William Irvine. His father, Asad Khan, became the long-serving wazir of Emperor Aurangzeb, and his mother, Mehrunissa Begum, was a daughter of Asaf Khan, wazir under Shah Jahan. The family was Iranian on the father's side: his grandfather had moved to India after his great-grandfather, the governor of Safavid Shirvan, was executed around 1600 by Shah Abbas I. In 1677 he married a daughter of the noble Shaista Khan and received the title Itiqad Khan.

In 1689 he captured the Maratha fort of Raigad. The Maratha king Rajaram Bhonsle escaped to Jinji, but the family of his predecessor Sambhaji, including the young Shahu, was taken, and Muhammad Ismail was given the title Zulfiqar Khan. Assigned in 1690 to the Siege of Jinji, he made slow progress against a strong fort and disrupted supply lines, and the length of the siege led contemporaries to accuse him of collusion with the enemy. In 1693 he and his father arrested Prince Kam Bakhsh for negotiating with Rajaram against orders. He became mir bakhshi, or paymaster general, in 1702.

In the war of succession of 1707 he reluctantly sided with Prince Azam Shah but deserted him at the Battle of Jajau. The victor, Bahadur Shah I, reconciled him, confirmed him as mir bakhshi and in 1709 made him governor of the Deccan. When Bahadur Shah lay dying in 1712, Zulfiqar Khan allied three of his sons against the strongest, Azim-us-Shan, and then helped Jahandar Shah, the weakest, to kill the others. For this the historian Munis Faruqui calls him the first kingmaker in Mughal history. As wazir he held effective power, abolished the jizya and continued to conciliate the Marathas.

Farrukhsiyar, a son of Azim-us-Shan, rebelled with the support of the Sayyid brothers and defeated Jahandar Shah at Agra in January 1713. The emperor sought shelter in Delhi at the house of Asad Khan, but father and son handed him over in the hope of winning the victor's favour. Despite assurances, Zulfiqar Khan was executed on 11 February 1713, and his body and that of Jahandar Shah were paraded on elephants and left before the Delhi Gate. According to Richard Eaton, his kingmaking set the precedent for power brokers raising puppet emperors to the Mughal throne.

notes: Birth year: the article gives 1649 (Chandra) or 1657 (Irvine); the existing entry has 1657 only.
The article says he was appointed faujdar of the Carnatic in 1692, not 'first Nawab of the Carnatic' as the existing description has it; I did not repeat either.
The spelling in the article is Jinji (the existing entry has Gingee).
